title: Abramovich arrives next door
detail: Chelsea's new owner bids for Henry; Arsenal's vice-chairman reacts.
people: David Dein; Roman Abramovich; Thierry Henry
evidence: Arsenal vice-chairman David Dein however was displeased, and quipped that Abramovich had "parked his Russian tanks on our lawn and is firing £50 notes at us", Abramovich was said to have placed a bid for Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, which was turned down at once.

title: Jens Lehmann replaces David Seaman
detail: The summer's only major signing (£1.5m from Borussia Dortmund; date from the season page's transfer table).
evidence: German goalkeeper Jens Lehmann was the only major addition to the first team; he replaced David Seaman who joined Manchester City.

title: The Battle of Old Trafford
detail: 0–0 at United. Vieira sent off in the 80th minute; six Arsenal players charged and a record £175,000 club fine.
people: Patrick Vieira; Ruud van Nistelrooy; Steve Bennett
evidence: Six of Arsenal's players (Ashley Cole, Lauren, Keown, Parlour, Lehmann, and Vieira) were later charged with improper conduct by The Football Association (FA), while the club were fined £175,000, the largest ever given to a club by the FA.

title: Cesc Fàbregas debuts at 16
detail: League Cup third round v Rotherham: 16 years and 177 days.
evidence: Wenger handed midfielder Cesc Fàbregas his debut at 16 years and 177 days.

title: Five at the San Siro
detail: Inter 1–5 Arsenal turns a Champions League campaign that started with a 0–3 home defeat to Inter.
evidence: In November, Arsenal beat Dynamo Kyiv by a single goal and more impressively scored five against Inter Milan at the San Siro – two results which kick-started their Champions League campaign.

title: José Antonio Reyes debuts
detail: Signed from Sevilla on 28 January for £10.5m; comes off the bench v Manchester City.
evidence: In a home match against Manchester City, Reyes made his first appearance for the club, coming on as a substitute in the second half.

title: Club record: 24 unbeaten from the start
detail: Wolves 1–3 Arsenal beats George Graham's 1990–91 record.
evidence: Arsenal recorded an away win at Wolverhampton Wanderers on 7 February 2004, their 24th league match, which bettered a club record of games unbeaten from the start of the season (originally held by George Graham's team of 1990–91).

title: Henry's 100th Premier League goal
evidence: Henry reached a personal landmark against Southampton three days later, scoring his 100th and 101st Premier League goals.

title: English record: 30 unbeaten from the start
detail: 1–1 with United at Highbury passes the record held by Leeds and Liverpool.
evidence: In avoiding defeat, Arsenal set a new all-time league record of 30 matches unbeaten from the start of the season, originally held by Leeds and Liverpool.

title: Bridge's late goal ends the European run
detail: Champions League quarter-final, second leg: Arsenal 1–2 Chelsea. Two cup exits in a week (FA Cup semi on 3 April).
evidence: With three minutes remaining of the match, defender Wayne Bridge scored to eliminate Arsenal from the competition.

title: Henry turns Good Friday around
detail: Liverpool lead 2–1 at half-time; two goals in a minute and a Henry hat-trick make it 4–2.
evidence: Arsenal responded by scoring twice in a minute; Henry's second goal saw the player hold off Dietmar Hamann in midfield, weave through defender Jamie Carragher, and place the ball past Jerzy Dudek.

title: Champions at White Hart Lane
detail: A 2–2 draw at Tottenham is enough.
evidence: With Chelsea unable to garner maximum points in their next two matches, Arsenal knew before their game away at Tottenham that a draw would guarantee their status as champions.

title: Unbeaten: 26 wins, 12 draws
detail: Arsenal 2–1 Leicester completes the league season without a defeat.
evidence: The club ended the Premier League campaign as champions without a single defeat – a record of 26 wins and 12 draws.

title: Open-top bus parade
evidence: A day after the Leicester City match, Arsenal paraded the Premier League trophy on an open-top bus, in front of more than 250,000 fans.

title: "The Invincibles"
detail: The nickname and the gold trophy.
evidence: They acquired the nickname "The Invincibles", much like the Preston North End team that went unbeaten in the inaugural Football League season (1888-89).

title: Henry's awards
detail: Players' Player and Footballer of the Year, both for the second season running; 39 goals in 51 games.
evidence: Henry was given the accolade of PFA Players' Player of the Year by his fellow peers and the FWA Footballer of the Year by football writers for the second consecutive season.

title: Epilogue: 49 unbeaten
detail: The run continues into 2004–05 and ends at Old Trafford.
evidence: The team eclipsed the league record of 42 matches without defeat (set by Nottingham Forest) against Blackburn Rovers and went seven more matches unbeaten until they lost – away to Manchester United in October 2004.
